facts.statement: The animal was discovered in Provence in 1992 following a forest fire.
facts.quote: It is known from a single partial specimen that was found in Provence in 1992, after a forest fire.

facts.statement: The species was named Pyroraptor olympius by Allain and Taquet in 2000.
facts.quote: The animal was named Pyroraptor olympius by Allain and Taquet in 2000.

facts.statement: The genus name means "fire thief" because the fossils were found after a 1992 forest fire.
facts.quote: The generic name comes from πῦρ (pûr, Greek for "fire") and raptor (Latin for "thief"), since its remains were discovered after a forest fire that occurred in 1992.

facts.statement: The specific name "olympius" is derived from Mont Olympe, the mountain near where the remains were found.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Mont Olympe, the mountain in Provence at the foot of which the animal's remains were unearthed.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of the left foot's second toe claw.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MNHN BO001, consists of the second toe claw of the left foot.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor was a small, bird-like dromaeosaurid with 6.6 cm long curved claws on its second toes.
facts.quote: Pyroraptor olympius was a dromaeosaurid, a small, bird-like predatory theropod that possessed enlarged curved claws on the second toe of each foot for predation; these claws were 6.6 cm long for Pyroraptor.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor's known teeth were flattened, curved backwards, and had finer serrations on the rear margins than the front.
facts.quote: Its two known teeth are flattened and curved backwards, with their rear margins having finer serrations than at the front.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor was covered in feathers, similar to its relatives Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus.
facts.quote: Pyroraptor was also covered in feathers, as many of its relatives, like Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus, also had plumage.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pyroraptor's enlarged claws may have been used as weapons or for climbing.
facts.quote: As in other dromaeosaurids, these claws might have been used as weapons or as climbing aids.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the known Pyroraptor remains belong to a single individual due to their disarticulated nature.
facts.quote: However, due to the disarticulated nature of Pyroraptor remains, it's unknown if they belong to the same individual.

facts.statement: A 2012 study argues that many traits considered unique to Pyroraptor are actually widespread among dromaeosaurids or caused by preservation deformation.
facts.quote: A 2012 study also agrees that Pyroraptor's "unique" traits are widespread features of dromaeosaurids, while also ruling out some of the other "unique traits" as results of preservation deformation.

facts.statement: The possibility that Pyroraptor and Variraptor are the same species is raised, but it cannot yet be tested due to a lack of overlapping fossil material.
facts.quote: Since the two existed at the same time and place, the possibility of a synonymy between Pyroraptor and Variraptor is raised but it is concluded that due to the current lack of overlap in material, this possible synonymy cannot yet be tested and more remains are needed.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor is known from fossils found in Provence, France.
facts.quote: It is known from a single partial specimen that was found in Provence in 1992, after a forest fire.

facts.statement: A single specimen of Pyroraptor was discovered in 1992 in Provence, southern France, consisting of only a few bones.
facts.quote: Un solo espécimen ha sido encontrado en 1992, en Provenza al sur de Francia y solo es conocido por unos cuantos huesos.

facts.statement: The species was named Pyroraptor olympius by paleontologists Ronan Allain and Philippe Taquet in 2000.
facts.quote: Llamado Pyroraptor olympius por Allain y Taquet en 2000.

facts.statement: The genus name means "fire thief" in Greek because the fossils were found after a forest fire.
facts.quote: El nombre del género en griego significa "ladrón de fuego", debido a que sus restos fueron descubiertos después de que ocurriera un incendio forestal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, MNHN BO001, consists of the left foot's second claw.
facts.quote: La muestra de holotipo, MNHN BO001, consiste en la segunda garra del pie izquierdo.

facts.statement: The first Pyroraptor remains were found in southeastern France at the locality of La Boucharde in the Arc Basin, Provence.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Pyroraptor se descubrieron en el sureste de Francia, en la localidad de La Boucharde de la Cuenca del Arco en Provenza.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Pyroraptor belongs to the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Dromaeosaurinae

facts.statement: The genus authority is Allain & Taquet, 2000.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Allain & Taquet, 2000

facts.statement: Pyroraptor is considered a "wildcard taxon" that creates instability in phylogenetic analyses unless it is removed.
facts.quote: Due to its status as a "wildcard taxon", Pyroraptor is known to create issues in phylogenies which are only fixed when it is pruned from the analysis.

facts.statement: A 2019 phylogenetic study suggested Pyroraptor might be an unenlagiine, a group of Gondwanan dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: In the 2019 description of Hesperornithoides, a phylogeny tree found Pyroraptor to be an unenlagiine.

facts.statement: A 2021 study ruled out Pyroraptor as an unenlagiine because its teeth differ significantly from those of unenlagiines.
facts.quote: The 2021 description of Ypupiara lopai rules out Pyroraptor as being an unenlagiine due to this dissimilarity.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, hace 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiano, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The time range for Pyroraptor is estimated from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Early evolutionary models suggested dromaeosaurids originated in North America or Euro-America and dispersed to Asia, but this model has since lost support.
facts.quote: During the initial description of Pyroraptor olympius, the suggested model of dromaeosaurid evolution proposed that the family originated from North America or Euro-America, and then dispersed into Asia.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor was a bipedal hunter with a sickle claw measuring 6.5 centimeters on the second toe of each foot.
facts.quote: Pyroraptor fue un cazador bípedo con una garra falciforme de 6,5 centímetros en el segundo dedo de cada pie.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor possessed long arms with sharp claws used to grip its prey.
facts.quote: Poseía, además, largos brazos con filosas garras para poder aferrarse de sus presas.

facts.statement: Its small and slender body shape indicates that Pyroraptor was a fast animal.
facts.quote: Su forma era pequeña y esbelta lo cual indica que era un animal veloz.

facts.statement: The two known teeth of Pyroraptor are flattened, curved backward, and have finer serrations on the posterior margins than on the front.
facts.quote: Sus dos dientes conocidos son aplanados y curvados hacia atrás, y sus márgenes posteriores tienen dentaduras más finas que las del frente.

facts.statement: It is probable that Pyroraptor was covered in feathers, as many of its relatives like Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus had plumage.
facts.quote: Es probable que Pyroraptor también estuviera cubierto de plumas, ya que muchos de sus parientes, como Microraptor y Sinornithosaurus, también tenían plumaje.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor is known from the Argiles et Grès à Reptiles Formation in what is now southern France.
facts.quote: Pyroraptor olympius is known from the Argiles et Grès à Reptiles Formation of what is now Southern France.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, Pyroraptor lived on the island landmass of Ibero-Armorica, formed from modern-day southern France and northern Spain in the Tethys Ocean.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous, it was one part of the island landmass known as Ibero-Armorica, formed from what is today Southern France and Northern Spain in the Tethys Ocean.

facts.statement: Pyroraptor coexisted with diverse species including the dinosaur Zalmoxes, the titanosaur Rhabdodon, the sauropod Ampelosaurus, the theropod Variraptor, the bird Martinaves, and various non-dinosaur reptiles like the pterosaur Azhdarcho and crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: At that time, Pyroraptor would have coexisted alongside a variety of species such as Zalmoxes, Rhabdodon priscus, Ampelosaurus atacis, Lirainosaurus astibiae, Atsinganosaurus velauciensis, some undescribed titanosaurids, Arcovenator escotae, Tarascosaurus salluvicus, Struthiosaurus sp., Variraptor mechanorum, Gargantuavis philoinos, Martinaves cruzyensis, and non-dinosaurs such as the pterosaurs Azhdarcho lancicollis and Hatzegopteryx thambema, the crocodylomorphs Musturzabalsuchus buffetauti, Massaliasuchus, and Allodaposuchus, the turtles Dortoka, and Solemydid turtles, zhelestid eutherians, palaeobatrachid anurans, batrachosauroidid urodeles, amphisbaenian and/or anguid squamates, and derived alethinophidian snakes.

facts.statement: A 2022 study noted that Pyroraptor's foot morphology resembles unenlagiines more than eudromaeosaurs, supporting the idea that European raptors were related to Southern Hemisphere forms.
facts.quote: The 2022 description of Vectiraptor greeni noted that the foot morphology of Pyroraptor olympius had more similarities with unenlagiines than with eudromaeosaurs, lending support to the idea that European raptors were closely related to Southern forms from Africa and South America.
